producer_report.summary: Planning now comes first. A plan (goal, ladder rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies, touched paths) is built for all open items together. The drain works items in plan order (ladder, then dependencies, then age) and not oldest first. It can stop at a job boundary with a distinct Requested stop reason. Items whose plan lacks goal, rung or acceptance are refused for design or code and reported. The fix for this send-back: the refusal behavior was already implemented and tested. I confirmed the drain test passes and reported it in criteria_check. The full cargo test --locked passes.

checks_run.note: order and refusal drain tests pass

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: an item whose plan lacks goal, ladder rung, or acceptance is refused for design or code and reported, so planning cannot be skipped.
criteria_check.evidence: Drain test an_item_whose_plan_lacks_goal_rung_or_acceptance_is_not_worked_and_is_reported (crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs): items a (no goal), b (no rung), c (no acceptance) are never read or run (log is only 'read d','run d','land d','rate'), they stay queued, report.refused names each with what is missing, and display output says 'the plan lacks acceptance'. Core test a_plan_without_goal_rung_or_acceptance_is_refused in plan.rs also passes. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain plan

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a drain test with three queued items where a newer item is planned first shows the drain works items in plan order, not oldest first.
Run cargo test: a drain test that requests a stop mid-run shows the loop finishes the current job, starts no further job, and reports a distinct stop reason (not a killed job).
criteria_check.evidence: Stop::Requested handled in drain loop; stop test in tests/drain.rs passes in the full run.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a plan built from several open items names, for each, goal, ladder rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies, and touched paths, and groups items with disjoint touches and no dependency as parallel while ordering dependent items after what they need.
criteria_check.evidence: plan.rs tests disjoint_independent_items_share_a_group_and_dependents_come_after pass; PlanEntry carries all fields.

criteria_check.criterion: The plan-stage audit from n2qb is described: each logged gap (intervention, introspection, rejection, rating) is traced to a stage (reading, decomposition, assumptions, criteria, outcome check), with a check of whether later gaps of that kind fell; if full automation is too large, the remainder is stated as follow-up.
criteria_check.evidence: plan.rs GapKind, Stage, trace, GapLog::fell with tests; design doc states the follow-up.

criteria_check.criterion: Docs (README, design doc, CHANGELOG) state the planning-first order and how to stop a drain at a job boundary, for an outside reader.
criteria_check.evidence: README, roles-and-ladder.md, CHANGELOG.md, decisions.md edited in earlier pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check: all pass, and no new unused or untested module.
criteria_check.evidence: cargo test --locked passes in full; plan module has tests and is used by drain.rs.

criteria_check.criterion: No design work for moving compute to CI is included; it is left for after this lands.

open_issues: Running plan groups in parallel is not implemented; the drain runs one job at a time in plan order.
The plan-stage audit is a first slice (trace plus fell check); wiring it to the real logs is follow-up.
I did not rerun clippy or fmt in this pass; they passed earlier.
mistakes: The earlier report left the refusal criterion out of criteria_check, though the test already existed.
learnings: Bash allows no pipes, so full test output is read without grep or tail; use cargo test -q.
